shipped_rows.title_o: Promoting Interest and Performance in High School Science Classes

blind_target.authors: Hulleman, C. S., Godes, O., Hendricks, B. L., & Harackiewicz, J. M.
blind_target.title: Enhancing interest and performance with a utility value intervention.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Although the research generated by the expectancy-value framework has been largely correlational (Wigfield & Cambria, 2010), recent classroom studies reveal that interventions designed to enhance perceptions of value can increase both interest and course perfor- mance (e.g., Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009; Hulleman, Godes, Hendricks, & Harackiewicz, 2010). The research presented herein replicates and extends this prior work by further investigating a theory-based intervention designed to enhance student motivation and performance.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The results of Study 2 partially replicated prior research dem- onstrating that a theoretically guided intervention based on the expectancy-value framework could enhance student learning out- comes (Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009; Hulleman et al., 2010).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly give a partial-replication verdict over both cited prior intervention papers; interest/performance benefits coexist with an unexpected mechanism.

prior_decision.quote: The utility value interventions utilized in the current studies were based on the self-generated utility value interventions used by Hulleman and colleagues (e.g., Hulleman et al., 2010; Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009). In addition to replicating this prior research, we extend it in five ways.
